correctness.rationale: With independent rate-1/n exponential first arrivals, an edge with two vacant endpoints cannot yet have rung, so memorylessness gives the three exact mass-action rates. On the invariant cube the polynomial drift is Lipschitz (it need not be globally Lipschitz on R^4); scaled counting martingales have quadratic variation O(T/n), which gives the fixed-time fluid limit by Doob and Gronwall. Balance yields b=(1-alpha)h, d=(1-beta)h and, with I'=h, a=alpha exp(-(1-beta)I), c=beta exp(-(1-alpha)I). Off the diagonal, balance gives the first zero of h at I*=log(beta/alpha)/(beta-alpha). On the diagonal, solving dh/dI=-(a+b) gives h=exp(-(1-alpha)I)(1-alpha I). In both cases h>0 before its first zero, so I tends to I* and the density tends to (r,0,r,0). The deterministic future-consumption bound by b_n(T)+d_n(T) makes the infinite-time transfer valid, and boundedness gives convergence in mean. Complement vacancies are in fact exactly zero at any finite graph's jam: either complement has edges to the entire opposite side, which would have a vacancy by balance. Class counts here are normalized by n. The perfect-matching construction is valid. As a finite check, for n=2 and one missing pair, exactly one of the three equiprobable first edges leaves a vacancy per side. This verifies the stated 1/3 for that case only; no frozen script was executed.
residual_risks: No joint limit with vanishing blocked proportions or quantitative finite-n convergence claimed or checked.
